result.flow_strategy: Reused T0036_v5 synth_ooc.dcp checkpoint, swapped XDC (4.0 -> 6.0 ns), re-ran opt + place + route. Same logic, only constraint relaxed.
result.achievable_fmax_basis: Fmax = 1000 / (6.0 + |WNS|) = 1000 / 6.473 = 154.5 MHz. Same critical path as v5 at 250 MHz target: u_sched/u_vision_fifo BRAM access, ~6.47 ns end-to-end delay regardless of clock target.
result.wns_diagnosis: v5 critical path was 5.378 ns of pure route delay on u_sched/u_vision_fifo BRAM. v6 with 6.0 ns target should have given +0.6 ns margin, but the router/physopt with relaxed constraint slightly relaxed the placement (less effort needed) so the critical path actually grew slightly to ~6.47 ns. NET RESULT: v5 and v6 are within ±10% of the same actual silicon Fmax (~154-158 MHz). The bottleneck is fundamental to the BD topology (long BRAM path in the multi-rate scheduler vision FIFO) — pipelining the scheduler is required to close timing at higher freqs.

Closing timing requires pipelining the FIFO (1-2 register stages on the write address / BRAM enable path).
